target_customer: Compliance, legal, risk and operations teams at regulated enterprises
problem: Tracking laws across jurisdictions and mapping changes to internal policies is manual. Regology offers a curated law library with change tracking and later AI agents.

founders.name: Mukund Goenka
founders.background_notes: YC page cites compliance, banking and enterprise software experience. TechCrunch coverage cited in a search result says over 15 years in banking; I did not open the article.

founders.name: Pavan Bayyapu
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as CTO with no background.

technical_complexity.rationale: Curating and normalizing laws across jurisdictions plus classification models was substantial data and NLP work.

defensibility.rationale: A curated law library takes time to build, but large legal publishers held similar content.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Bloomberg Industry Group, a legal and tax publisher, acquired Regology in June 2026.

market_need_then: Regulatory change management was an established compliance spend and RegTech vendors such as Compliance.ai (founded 2016 per one listing) existed. No dated 2018 demand figures were found.

branding.domain_note: regology.com, an exact .com; an early trademark record shows a REGOLOGY mark cancelled in 2017.

identity.mascot_or_character: Reggi, a generative AI assistant, is named in a trademark filed 2025

rebrands.why: Product page now carries the Bloomberg name after acquisition

brand_strength.rationale: Trademark filings and product naming exist, but no press about the brand itself and the name is easily confused with Regnology, a different company.

outcome_analysis: Regology grew from a 2017 San Francisco startup to about 60 people, raised an 8 million dollar Series A in 2021 and added AI agents on a curated Smart Law Library. Bloomberg Industry Group acquired it in June 2026, which fits an incumbent legal publisher buying a regulatory AI wedge. Price and total funding are not public, so success is judged only by the exit.
notes: Series A came from search results across several outlets (fintech.global, FinSMEs, Grit Daily, TechCrunch) with the Business Wire release; I could not open the Business Wire or Bloomberg pages (403), so details rest on those snippets. A separate page gave 2021-06 with a 30 million pre-money; that is unverified and not recorded. Aggregators list Y Combinator, VentureSouq and GMO as investors; unverified. No seed round was found. Do not confuse with Regnology. A dated 2018 competitor search returned only current listings, so the list is empty.
